sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x. Languoid page 'Southern Guiyang Hmong' sout1555 and reference 62626.
sources.note: Lists a single descriptive source (Li 1993, type phonology, Mandarin, pp. 29-37); the Guiyang node (guiy1235) shows only Niederer 1998 and Johnson 2002 subclassification comments.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Family-level only. §4.2.1 (p. 199): Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached'. p. 28 quotes Downer 1961 on Mien reduced syllables with 'weaker stress and shorter duration' giving iambic rhythm. No statement about Guiyang Miao word stress.

sources.citation: Mortensen, David R. 2006. Logical and substantive scales in phonology. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.note: Guiyang mentioned only in Western Hmongic subgrouping remarks; stress discussion concerns other languages (Jingpho, English reduplication). Nothing on Guiyang Miao stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Guiyang Miao language' and (zh) '贵阳苗语' wikitext (citing Wang 1985, Li 2000, Li 2018, Mortensen 2004, Ly Van Tu & Vittrant 2014).
sources.note: No phonology. Gives the dialect table (Li 2018 populations, Wang 1985 datapoints): South [hmy] 20,000+, Anshun & Zhenning, datapoint Wangjiashan, Huayan, Anshun; Northwest 6,000, Qingzhen/Qianxi/Longlin, datapoint Tieshi, Qianxi.

sources.citation: 王辅世 Wang Fushi (ed.). 1985. 苗语简志. Beijing: 民族出版社.

sources.note: Standard sketch of Miao by subdialect; describes the Guiyang subdialect including the South vernacular (datapoint Wangjiashan, Huayan, Anshun) that corresponds to Ethnologue/ISO hmy; 简志 volumes normally include a short statement on 轻重音/轻声 in the phonology chapter.
